claims.text: Selective oxidation of individual elements governs oxidation resistance and high-temperature material integrity in multiprincipal-element alloys.
CrMnFeCoNi preferentially oxidizes Mn at high temperature.
Mn oxidation in CrMnFeCoNi forms non-protective oxides and depletes the bulk alloy of Mn.
The Mn-rich oxides do not limit further oxygen diffusion and therefore cause rapid degradation.
Partially replacing Mn with Al or increasing Cr promotes stable, adherent, self-healing Al2O3 and/or Cr2O3 scales.
A dense Al2O3 and/or Cr2O3 scale acts as an oxygen-diffusion barrier and preserves the underlying alloy microstructure.
Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi is a single-phase multiprincipal-element alloy.
High-temperature oxidation of CrMnFeCoNi produces predominantly Mn-rich oxides.
The relevant service-like exposure is sustained oxidation in air at approximately 750–1320 °C.
The governing structural mediator is the composition, structure, coherence, and adhesion of the surface oxide scale.
Reducing Mn and adding Al or Cr will lower oxidation rate, as measured by reduced mass gain over time relative to CrMnFeCoNi.
The modified alloy will form a more coherent and protective oxide scale than baseline CrMnFeCoNi.
The modified alloy will retain mechanical properties better after long-term high-temperature oxidation than baseline CrMnFeCoNi.
The hypothesis applies from roughly 750 °C to 1320 °C where the single-phase solid solution remains stable.
Applicability to molten salts or substantially different temperature regimes is uncertain.
The quantitative benefit depends on the precise composition and processing route, while effects of grain boundaries and secondary phases remain unresolved.
A controlled comparison should expose baseline CrMnFeCoNi and a Mn-reduced, Al-added and/or Cr-enriched alloy to identical air oxidation at about 800 °C.
Mass gain, oxide phase and composition, oxide morphology, and post-oxidation mechanical properties are measurable discriminating outcomes.
Failure of the modified alloy to reduce oxidation rate, form a coherent protective scale, or improve mechanical retention relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
